tech.name: Claude Ship (Code Review + PR Steward + Claude Approvals)
tech.released: 2026-11-23, beta (PR Steward, Claude Approvals); Code Review generally available
tech.status: beta on Claude Team and Enterprise plans, GitHub repositories
tech.one_line: Agents that take a GitHub pull request through review, fixes and an approval decision: PR Steward works on failing checks, merge conflicts and review feedback; Claude Approvals can approve routine changes on its own when the team's policy file allows it.

predecessor.name: An AI review that only left comments: the developer fixed failing checks, conflicts and comments by hand, and every pull request waited for a person to approve it (the counted example is the episode's own)

claims.text: Claude Ship launched November 23, 2026, in beta: Claude can review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones a team's policy allows
Claude Ship = Code Review (generally available) + two new beta agents, PR Steward and Claude Approvals, taking a PR through review, fixes and an approval decision
Before: the review comes back, you stop, dig back into the old code, push a fix, wait for the review again, then find someone to approve it
Most teams want a person to approve every change
PR Steward jumps in on failing CI checks, merge conflicts and review feedback; it is designed not to approve or merge
PR Steward comments after every push with what it changed and how to undo it
PR Steward attempts to fix failing checks (when the cause is in code the PR touches) and resolve merge conflicts; you can start your next change while it works
Claude Approvals applies a policy file the team writes in the repo; Claude can approve routine changes on its own if the policy allows it, or require human sign-off
The policy can ask more people for risky changes and fewer for routine ones (billing code two people; test fixtures one once Code Review passes); file .claude/approvals.yml
Anthropic recommends observe-only mode first; the check blocks merges only where it is a required GitHub check
Claude Ship uses AI and may miss bugs, security vulnerabilities, or other issues
On the Claude Code team, where Claude's review is one layer of a broader process, merged PRs more than doubled from June to September
A docs fix: Code Review found nothing blocking, a docs reviewer signed off, Claude Approvals passed, and it merged the same evening
Available on Claude Team and Enterprise plans for GitHub repositories; not with Zero Data Retention, HIPAA configuration or customer-managed keys
Billed on tokens, so turning it on can add to costs
TechCrunch confirms: an agent that can approve code changes automatically based on policies set by a development team
